newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq bought additional 100,000 T French wheat.
newsitem.headline: Iraq bought additional 100,000 T French wheat.

text.p: Iraq has bought an additional 100,000 tonnes of French wheat, lifting its total purchases of French wheat under the United Nations oil-for-food agreement to 300,000 tonnes, European grain traders said on Friday.
The French wheat for January-February delivery was priced at $200 per tonne cost and freight for delivery to Jordan's port of Aqaba, they said.
Additional costs linked to the transport by truck of the grain to Baghdad, put the purchase at $230 per tonne, delivery Baghdad.
On Thursday grain traders said Iraq had bought 200,000 tonnes of French wheat for January and February, plus 100,000 tonnes from Australia.
The French wheat was priced according to gluten content at $194.85, $198.05 and $199.85 per tonne and was for delivery to the Iraqi port of Umm Qasr.
Earlier on Friday the Australian Wheat Board said 250,000 tonnes of Australian wheat wheat had been sold to Iraq for January-February delivery.
This would put at 550,000 tonnes total wheat purchases made so far by Iraq under the oil-for-food scheme.
